evals.name: review-planted-correctness-and-perf
evals.prompt:
Please review this Haskell module.

```haskell
module Worker where

import Prelude

data Config = Config { configHost :: String, configRetries :: Int }

sumFile :: FilePath -> IO Int
sumFile path = do
  contents <- readFile path
  let ns = map read (lines contents)
  pure (foldl (+) 0 ns)

firstLine :: FilePath -> IO String
firstLine path = do
  contents <- readFile path
  pure (head (lines contents))
```

assertions: Flags the partial functions `head` and `read` used in production code
Flags lazy `Prelude.readFile` and recommends Data.Text.IO / ByteString equivalents

evals.name: review-transformer-stack-and-env
evals.prompt:
Review the application-monad design in this module.

```haskell
module App where

import Control.Monad.Except
import Control.Monad.State
import Control.Monad.Reader

data Env = Env
  { envPool  :: Pool Connection
  , envUsers :: IORef [User]
  }

newtype App a = App (ExceptT Err (StateT Cache (ReaderT Env IO)) a)
  deriving (Functor, Applicative, Monad)
```
evals.expected_output: Flags the deep transformer stack -> newtype over ReaderT Env IO; StateT -> IORef/TVar in env; ExceptT -> exceptions in IO caught at boundaries; mutable business state in env (envUsers :: IORef [User]) -> env should hold resources, not business data; non-strict env fields. Bonus: Has-pattern / runApp.
assertions: Flags the deep transformer stack and recommends a newtype over `ReaderT Env IO`
Flags `StateT` and recommends an IORef/TVar in the environment instead
Flags `ExceptT` and recommends throwing exceptions in IO, caught at boundaries
Flags mutable business state in the env (envUsers :: IORef [User]) — env should hold resources, not business data
Bonus: notes non-strict env fields and/or the Has-pattern / missing runApp

evals.name: review-idiomatic-no-false-positives
evals.prompt:
Review this module.

```haskell
module Domain.User where

import qualified Data.Text as T
import Data.Text (Text)
import Data.Int (Int64)

newtype UserId = UserId { unUserId :: Int64 }
  deriving newtype (Eq, Ord, Show)

data Role = Admin | Editor | Viewer
  deriving stock (Eq, Ord, Show)

newtype Email = Email { unEmail :: Text }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)

mkEmail :: Text -> Either Text Email
mkEmail t
  | T.isInfixOf (T.pack "@") t = Right (Email t)
  | otherwise                 = Left (T.pack "invalid email")

data User = User
  { _user_id    :: !UserId
  , _user_role  :: !Role
  , _user_email :: !Email
  }
  deriving stock (Eq, Show)
```
evals.expected_output: This code already follows the skill's guidance (newtype ids, sum type for Role, smart constructor for Email, strict type-prefixed fields, explicit DerivingStrategies, Text not String). A good review recognizes it is largely idiomatic and does NOT invent spurious bugs; any suggestions are minor/genuine, not fabricated problems.
assertions: Recognizes the code is largely idiomatic and correct (does not claim it is broken)
Does NOT fabricate spurious correctness/performance issues (no false flags about partiality, foldl, String, etc. that aren't present)
Any suggestions offered are genuine, minor improvements rather than nitpicks or invented problems
